results.title: How to build or migrate an AI agent with AWS Startup Advisor
results.content:
## What makes AWS Startup Advisor unique?

Ask an LLM to suggest an agent architecture and you can get a plausible answer in seconds. However, this is often generic, inconsistent on AWS specifics, and untested against your workload.

Turning a suggestion into a deployable solution requires decisions about AWS services, configuration, costs, and how different components work together. AWS Startup Advisor is designed to take those workload-specific requirements into account when making recommendations. [...] ## Phase 3: Design

AWS Startup Advisor does not hand back a menu of options; it makes one recommendation and explains why. A deterministic scoring engine first rules out runtimes that will not fit the workload, then ranks what remains on how the agent actually runs (session length, orchestration, traffic shape, ops preference, and existing infrastructure), and records why each was chosen or eliminated:

Runtime scores: AgentCore 44 | Lambda MicroVMs 41 | ECS 33 | EKS 28  
 Eliminated: Lambda Standard (15-min timeout cannot cover 15min-8hr sessions) [...] There are options to suit any use case or budget, but how do you decide which combination is the right fit for your startup? AWS Startup Advisor simplifies the decision, analyzing your workload and recommending an architecture across the agent stack.

If you have an existing agent, the challenge is slightly different: how do you move what you already have to AWS without rebuilding it unnecessarily? Memory, guardrails, tools, and other parts of an agent can be tied to the platform they were built on, so migration may require changes across the stack. AWS Startup Advisor maps those components to AWS and identifies where changes are needed.

results.content:
## What is AWS Startup Advisor?

AWS Startup Advisor is your AI-powered build assistant, available as an extension for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, and Kiro or as a standalone experience on the web. It gives you and your coding agents tailored guidance on AI, architecture, costs, credits, security, and migration, matched to your startup's stack and stage. Whether you're starting from an idea or moving an existing app to AWS, it meets you where you build and adapts its recommendations as your startup grows. AWS Startup Advisor doesn't store your code or share your data with third parties.

## How does it work? [...] ## Does it include proactive alerts?

Yes. The Alerts tab in the IDE extension surfaces optimization opportunities and recommended actions. It uses your AWS profile permissions to monitor configured resources and proactively flag what to fix, so you stay ahead of issues.

Let us know so we can improve the quality of the content on our pages [...] ## How does it work?

AWS Startup Advisor picks up where your AWS Activate Credit application leaves off. It uses your application data and your startup’s website to understand your stack and stage. From there, it delivers guidance through a skills-based experience: scaffold an architecture, optimize costs, set up your environment, migrate to AWS, or deploy an AI agent. Each step is shaped by what you’re actually building.

## How much does it cost?

AWS Startup Advisor is available at no additional charge. You pay only for the AWS resources you or your agent provisions or interacts with, at standard AWS pricing.

# What is AWS Startup Advisor?

AWS Startup Advisor is an AI-powered build assistant for startups. It provides AWS-vetted, Solutions Architect-curated skills and guidance for startups on account setup, architecture, Activate credits, cost, security, migration, AI, and scalability. AWS Startup Advisor delivers this guidance as skills that founders and their coding agents can use. You receive recommendations directly in your development environment, so you can act on them as you build.

This guide is for startup founders and startup developers who build on AWS. You can use AWS Startup Advisor at any stage, whether you are building your product from scratch, have an existing product or service you are enhancing or scaling, or if you are migrating from another cloud provider to AWS. [...] ## How AWS Startup Advisor uses your startup context

AWS Startup Advisor can pick up where your AWS Activate credit application leaves off. Instead of starting from scratch, if you applied for AWS Activate credits, you start with context about your startup. AWS Startup Advisor uses two sources to understand your tech stack and your startup’s stage:

 The information in your AWS Activate credit application
 Your startup’s website

AWS Startup Advisor combines this context with expertise from AWS Startup Solutions Architects. As a result, the guidance that you receive is tailored to your startup’s stack and stage.
